channel.title: How Biscuit
channel.description: Practical, evidence-aware guides for technology, home, kitchens, shopping decisions, and useful tools.

item.title: How Long Can Butter Sit Out?
item.description: Learn how long ordinary commercial butter can remain at room temperature, how to store it, and which butter products should remain refrigerated.

item.title: How Long Does Cooked Pasta Last in the Fridge?
item.description: Store cooked pasta safely for three to four days, cool it promptly, and learn when temperature, sauce, storage history, or spoilage means it should be discarded.

item.title: How to Recycle Lithium-Ion Batteries Safely
item.description: Prepare ordinary lithium-ion batteries for recycling and handle swollen, damaged, defective, or recalled batteries without putting them in household trash or curbside recycling.

item.title: Why Did My Garlic Turn Blue or Green?
item.description: Learn why garlic turns blue or green in vinegar, lemon, pickles, and acidic cooking, when the color is harmless, and how to distinguish it from mold.

item.title: Why Does My Phone Battery Drain Overnight?
item.description: Diagnose overnight battery drain on an iPhone or Android phone by checking background activity, cellular signal, updates, battery health, and application usage.

item.title: Why Is My Toilet Bubbling or Gurgling?
item.description: Diagnose a bubbling toilet by checking for a local clog, blocked vent, multiple slow drains, a restricted sewer line, or temporary municipal sewer work.

item.title: Why Is My Window Air Conditioner Leaking Water Inside?
item.description: Diagnose a window air conditioner leaking indoors by checking its outward slope, filter, ice buildup, drainage path, base pan, and window installation.

item.title: Apartment Move-In Inspection Checklist: Document Damage Before You Unpack
item.description: Inspect every room before moving furniture inside. Photograph existing damage, test essential systems, and submit the condition report on time.

item.title: Can a 100-Watt USB-C Charger Damage Your Phone?
item.description: A 100-watt USB-C laptop charger can usually charge a compatible phone safely. Learn how power negotiation works and which warning signs matter.

item.title: Can You Paint Over Mold?
item.description: Paint can hide mold temporarily, but it does not remove the growth or fix the moisture that caused it. Clean, dry, and repair the area first.

item.title: Can You Put Glass in the Freezer?
item.description: Glass can go in the freezer only when the container is intended for freezing, undamaged, not overfilled, and protected from sudden temperature changes.

item.title: How to Check for Recalls Before Buying a Used Product
item.description: A used product can look perfect and still be recalled. Search the exact model, serial number, production date, or VIN before paying.

item.title: How to Compare Unit Prices When Package Sizes Are Different
item.description: Compare different package sizes by dividing final checkout cost by usable quantity, converting to the same unit, and accounting for discounts, waste, and product differences.

item.title: Contractor Estimate Comparison Checklist
item.description: Compare written scope, materials, exclusions, schedule, licensing, insurance, permits, payment terms, warranties, and change-order rules instead of choosing only by total price.

item.title: How to Find and Stop Drafts Around Windows and Doors
item.description: Locate the exact moving joint or fixed crack before sealing it. Use weatherstripping on operable edges and caulk on stationary gaps.

item.title: Home Inventory Checklist: Document Your Belongings Before a Loss
item.description: Photograph every room, record valuable items and serial numbers, preserve receipts, store a copy away from home, and update the inventory after major purchases.

item.title: How Long Do Hard-Boiled Eggs Last in the Fridge?
item.description: Refrigerate hard-boiled eggs within two hours and use them within one week. Store them at 40°F or below.

item.title: How to Clean a Window Air Conditioner Filter
item.description: A dirty window-air-conditioner filter restricts airflow and can reduce cooling performance. This guide explains the safe cleaning sequence for most reusable filters.

item.title: How to Spot a Fake Online Review
item.description: No single clue proves a review is fake. Compare sources, timing, reviewer history, incentives, listing changes, and recurring product-specific details.

item.title: Is It Safe to Leave a Laptop Plugged In All the Time?
item.description: Modern laptops should stop active charging at their target level, but prolonged time at full charge and high temperature can accelerate battery aging.

item.title: Power Outage Home Checklist: What to Do Before, During, and After
item.description: Keep the refrigerator closed, use flashlights instead of candles, operate generators outdoors, and inspect food and equipment when power returns.

item.title: Return Policy vs. Warranty vs. Service Contract: What Actually Protects You?
item.description: A return policy, product warranty, and service contract address different problems. Learn what each protects and what to inspect before paying extra.

item.title: How to Spot a Fake Online Store Before You Buy
item.description: Verify the exact domain, research the seller independently, compare prices, read return and shipping terms, and avoid payment methods that make recovery difficult.

item.title: Why Is My Bathroom Exhaust Fan Dripping Water?
item.description: Water dripping from a bathroom exhaust fan usually comes from condensation inside a cold duct or leakage around the exterior roof or wall vent.

item.title: Why Does Bluetooth Keep Disconnecting?
item.description: Repeated Bluetooth drops usually come from low accessory power, distance, competing paired devices, stale pairing data, power-saving settings, software problems, or failing hardware.

item.title: Why Bread Goes Stale Faster in the Refrigerator
item.description: Refrigeration can slow mold, but ordinary refrigerator temperatures accelerate the starch changes that make bread firm and stale.

item.title: Why Do Onions Make You Cry?
item.description: Cutting an onion ruptures its cells and starts an enzyme-driven reaction that releases a volatile sulfur compound, causing the eyes to produce tears.

item.title: Why Does My Faucet Keep Dripping?
item.description: A drip from the spout usually means an internal seal, washer, cartridge, valve seat, or ceramic component is no longer sealing.

item.title: Why Is My Laptop Fan So Loud?
item.description: A loud laptop fan usually means heavy processor activity or restricted airflow. This guide separates normal cooling noise from software, dust, and hardware trouble.

item.title: Why Is My Microwave Sparking?
item.description: Stop the microwave immediately. Common causes include metal, foil, metallic trim, burned food residue, an incorrectly positioned rack, empty operation, or cavity damage.

item.title: Why Does My Phone Get Hot While Charging?
item.description: Some warmth is normal during charging, especially with fast charging. Persistent excessive heat, swelling, odors, or a hot connector require attention.

item.title: Why Does My Toilet Keep Running?
item.description: A running toilet usually means water is leaking past the flapper or the fill system is sending water into the overflow tube. A dye test can identify the path.

item.title: Should You Wash Raw Chicken Before Cooking It?
item.description: No. Washing raw chicken can spread bacteria through splashing and does not replace cooking poultry to a safe internal temperature.

item.title: Can You Freeze Eggs?
item.description: How to freeze raw egg whites or whole eggs safely without putting shell eggs in the freezer.

item.title: Can You Freeze Milk?
item.description: You can freeze pasteurized milk in a freezer-safe container with expansion space, then thaw it in the refrigerator. Texture may separate, so shake or blend it after thawing.

item.title: Can You Mix Bleach and Vinegar?
item.description: Never mix chlorine bleach and vinegar. The combination can release toxic chlorine gas. Leave the area for fresh air and contact emergency or poison help if exposure occurs.

item.title: Can You Plug an Air Conditioner Into an Extension Cord?
item.description: A room air conditioner should normally plug directly into a grounded wall outlet, not an extension cord. Here is the safe response when its factory cord will not reach.

item.title: Can You Put Dish Soap in a Dishwasher?
item.description: Why ordinary hand-washing liquid does not belong in an automatic dishwasher and what to do after an accidental dose.

item.title: Do You Have to Preheat the Oven?
item.description: Preheat for most baking and whenever a recipe or package says to. Some roasts and casseroles can start in a cold oven, but food-safety temperatures still govern doneness.

item.title: Does Unplugging Appliances Save Electricity?
item.description: How standby power works, which devices are practical to switch off, and why measurement beats a universal savings claim.

item.title: How Long Does Cooked Rice Last in the Fridge?
item.description: Refrigerate cooked rice within two hours and use it within four days. Cool it promptly in shallow containers and reheat leftovers to 165°F.

item.title: How Often Should You Test and Replace Smoke Alarms?
item.description: Test smoke alarms at least monthly and replace the whole alarm when it is 10 years old, or sooner if its instructions or failed tests require it.

item.title: Is Freezer Burn Safe to Eat?
item.description: What freezer burn means, why it affects quality more than safety, and when a damaged package calls for a different decision.

item.title: Router Restart vs. Reset: What’s the Difference?
item.description: Why restarting a router is a low-risk first step while a factory reset erases personalized settings and requires setup again.

item.title: What Temperature Should a Freezer Be?
item.description: The safe freezer target, how to measure it, and what to check when the compartment runs warmer than expected.

item.title: What Temperature Should a Refrigerator Be?
item.description: Keep the refrigerator at 40°F or below and the freezer at 0°F. Verify the actual temperature with an appliance thermometer and allow air to circulate.

item.title: Why Does My Dishwasher Leave a White Film on Dishes?
item.description: White film on dishwasher loads is often mineral residue or detergent film, but permanent glass etching can look similar. Use a simple wipe test, then adjust water, detergent, and rinse aid.

item.title: Why Does My GFCI Outlet Keep Tripping?
item.description: A GFCI that keeps tripping may be detecting leakage current, moisture, a faulty appliance, or a wiring problem. Use this safe isolation sequence before calling an electrician.

item.title: Why Is My Dishwasher Not Drying Dishes?
item.description: A model-aware checklist for wet dishes, including cycle settings, rinse aid, loading, plastics, and signs that service may be needed.

item.title: Why Is My Refrigerator Sweating?
item.description: How humidity, door openings, gasket gaps, blocked vents, and temperature problems can cause moisture inside or outside a refrigerator.
